children: A Houthi missile attack caused minor damage to Saudi Aramco’s (
) offices in Riyadh’s financial district on Sunday, renewing security concerns in the capital. No injuries or deaths were reported, according to the Saudi Press Agency.

For investors, the strike highlights risks to Saudi Arabia’s efforts to attract foreign capital and expand beyond oil. Continued attacks could disrupt business travel and corporate operations while adding pressure to government finances already strained by conflict and a widening budget deficit.
The Iran-backed Yemeni group claimed responsibility for the assault. Saudi authorities said they subsequently destroyed two missile launchers used in attempted attacks.

The King Abdullah Financial District, or KAFD, houses the kingdom’s sovereign wealth fund, stock exchange and offices of international firms including Goldman Sachs and Brookfield. Remote-work requirements were in effect during the attack, limiting the immediate impact. Plans to reopen offices had been reversed Saturday.

The incident followed deadly strikes on Riyadh’s airport roughly a month earlier. Flight restrictions remain in place, while major events have been postponed or canceled, complicating Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman’s economic development plans.

Aramco’s infrastructure has faced increasingly frequent threats, including its Ras Tanura oil hub and East-West pipeline. The company has said it plans to expand pipeline capacity and increase overseas oil storage to reduce exposure to disruptions.

title: Houthi strike damages Aramco offices in Riyadh, raising business risks
